title: Implement two-queue scheduling with aging for mixed short/long prompts
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context
Mixed prompt-length distributions are causing head-of-line blocking in the current continuous batching scheduler (long prefill / long-context requests dominate selection and inflate tail latency for short prompts). This ticket implements the core two-queue dispatch policy with aging/starvation prevention.

Goal
Reduce user-visible p95 tail latency for short prompts under mixed workload (e.g., 80/20 short/long and long-spike scenarios) while guaranteeing progress for long prompts and avoiding throughput regression beyond acceptable limits.

Scope (this ticket)
- Implement a two-queue dispatch policy (short + long classes) with:
  - queueing primitives and selection logic (pick-next)
  - aging / starvation prevention
  - guardrails (max skew / burst caps) at the scheduler decision layer
- Integrate with existing batch-builder hooks so that selection works for both prefill and decode stages (without requiring full refactor).
- Add simulation-based checks if feasible (lightweight, deterministic) to catch starvation regressions.

Out of scope
- Full token budgeting enforcement (tracked separately; see ENG-2441/ENG-???? and PR follow-ups)
- Multi-tenant QoS productization

Design notes (implementation)
1) Classification assumption
- Requests are already classified short/long by ENG-2432 and stored on request context as scheduling_class = {SHORT,LONG}.
- For safety, treat unknown/missing class as LONG.

2) Two-queue mechanics
- Maintain two FIFO queues per scheduler instance:
  - short_q: latency-sensitive
  - long_q: throughput-sensitive
- Primary bias: prefer short_q.
- Progress guarantee for long_q using aging + max-wait:
  - Each request has enqueue_ts.
  - Compute long_effective_age_ms = now - long_q.front.enqueue_ts (or oldest long).
  - If long_effective_age_ms >= long_max_wait_ms => force service from long_q (subject to feasibility constraints).

3) Aging function / fairness
We discussed two variants:
A) Hard max-wait override (simple + auditable)
B) Continuous aging score (more flexible, but harder to reason about)
Implementation uses A + a small soft-share cap (burst cap) to avoid pathological long starvation even when short traffic is constant.

Parameters (config knobs wired later via config plumbing PR, but defaults live in code for prototype):
- long_max_wait_ms (default 250ms for hosted; 500ms for dedicated; tuned in benchmarks)
- short_burst_limit (default 8): maximum consecutive short selections when long_q non-empty
- long_force_min_batch (default 1): allow a long prefill to start even if it reduces batch packing efficiency (guarded)

4) Guardrails
- Avoid selecting long requests that would violate existing admission/backpressure constraints.
- If forced-long triggers but long request is temporarily infeasible (e.g., memory/KV constraints), record a counter and fall back to short; do not deadlock.
- When both queues are non-empty, enforce short_burst_limit to cap skew.

5) Prefill vs decode
- Prefill selection uses the two-queue policy.
- Decode path remains dominated by active sequences; however, the decision of which new requests to admit into the active set (prefill) is the lever for tail latency.
- We avoid changing token-level decode scheduling in this ticket; hooks added in later PR (see PR-24857) to reduce long-prefill dominance.

Testing / validation
- Unit tests:
  - Ensures FIFO ordering within each class.
  - Ensures long requests are serviced within long_max_wait_ms + epsilon under sustained short arrivals (simulated time).
  - Ensures burst cap triggers a long selection when long_q non-empty.
  - Ensures no infinite loop when forced-long is infeasible (falls back and increments counter).
- Simulation-based check (lightweight):
  - Deterministic queueing sim with a synthetic arrival process (e.g., short every 5ms, long every 50ms) and service quanta.
  - Assertion: max long wait bounded; short p95 not worse than baseline FIFO in the same sim.
  - Note: we’re not trying to predict real perf, only prevent starvation regressions.

Acceptance criteria
- Functional correctness:
  - No starvation for long requests under sustained short arrivals (bounded wait in tests and load test).
  - No regressions in scheduler stability (no busy loops; no deadlocks).
- Performance (benchmarks tracked in ENG-2449 / results doc):
  - Mixed 80/20 short/long: p95 latency improvement for short requests (target >= 15% on A100/H100 pools) with throughput regression <= 3%.
  - Long-only workload: throughput regression <= 2%.

- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-short-long-prompt-scheduling-policy.json
- Related PRs:

  - sources/github/redwood/pr-24905-fix-long-queue-starvation-edge-case.json (follow-up fix)
  - sources/github/redwood/pr-24857-prefill-decode-separation-hooks.json (related refactor)
  - sources/github/redwood/pr-24872-scheduler-token-budget-guardrails.json (guardrails follow-up)

Rollout
- Feature flagged; default OFF.
- Enabled only in perf canary first, then limited region/pool canary (ENG-2470).
comments: 2025-12-04 (Talia Benson): Creating core implementation ticket. Please keep this scoped to dispatch policy + starvation prevention. Token-budget guardrails can land separately if needed.

2025-12-06 (Lena Fischer): Reviewed the design section. Preference is hard max-wait + burst cap for prototype (simpler to reason about). Please add a deterministic sim/unit test that fails if long can starve when short is constant.

2025-12-08 (Marcus Reed): Started implementation in a branch. Plan: implement SchedulerQueues {short,long} with a pick_next() that takes now_ms + consecutive_short counter. Will add stats counters for forced-long and forced-long-infeasible; metrics emission is separate ticket but counters should exist.

2025-12-09 (Omar El-Sayed): Watch out for memory feasibility checks when forcing long prefill. If long request can’t allocate KV, don’t spin; fall back to short and increment a counter so we can see it in canary.

2025-12-11 (Hiro Tanaka): Kernel team note: don’t change decode scheduling in this PR unless necessary; mixing decode + prefill selection heuristics can cause kernel selection instability. Prefill admission is the right lever for now.

2025-12-13 (Marcus Reed): Opened PR for review: pr-24844-two-queue-dispatch-policy. Includes burst cap + max-wait override; adds unit tests with fake clock. Sim check is included as a deterministic test (not perf).

2025-12-16 (Lena Fischer): Review feedback on PR: the max-wait trigger should be based on oldest long request (not just front if we ever reorder). Also add coverage for the case where forced-long is infeasible due to transient constraints.

2025-12-18 (Marcus Reed): Addressed review comments; also added a regression test for forced-long infeasible fallback. Merged pr-24844. Filing follow-up after seeing a starvation edge case under sustained short + long-spike in load test.

2026-01-05 (Marcus Reed): Follow-up fix landed: pr-24905-fix-long-queue-starvation-edge-case. Root cause: consecutive_short counter reset on certain scheduler re-entries causing burst cap to never trip under specific prefill/decode interleaving. Added regression test.

2026-01-16 (Sofia Ivanova): Marking ENG-2438 Done. Core two-queue policy is in; further tuning/guardrails continue in token budget PR and benchmarking tasks. Please keep an eye on perf-canary once mixed scenarios roll out.
